description: Mira Mahmoud, first-year stemer. I love teamwork and exploration.
summary:
AstraCare is an autonomous offline AI-powered health companion made especially for deep-space exploration to deal with the 20-minute delay in talking and communication to Earth.
We developed an on-board smart tablet system that has a simple color-coded way to show the human body. Using Data Fusion, AstraCare deals with all 5 NASA hazards at the same time. It connects the astronauts' body data from suit sensors with the spaceship's information, like radiation levels and CO₂ in the cabin.
Unlike traditional health care on Earth, or waiting for help, AstraCare works completely without internet. It acts as an independent onboard doctor on the spaceship, predicting physical and psychological stress. It finds problems early on the body or mind. Gives quick, actionable, and medical guidance and advice. It is very important for the mission. It helps astronauts stay safe in control and fully protected during long-duration trips to Mars.
details:
Our project works on indicating and monitoring astronauts' health care during their missions. It indicates their heart rate, oxygen percentage, blood sugar, blood pressure, sleep duration, mood, and microgravity effects, providing a motion reminder and space location in order to determine the amount of exposure to radiation, and our project presents an aid that speeds up the communication, which is an offline AI assistant that send the asked questions and answers that the astronaunt asked in an instant in order to predict the case that the astronaunt might be facing to solve or prevent any risks or critical conditions.

Advantages of our project:

1) Monitor their health, resulting in prediction of exposure to any critical conditions or disease.

2) Will work as a tool guide for the astronauts in case of facing an emergency.

3) Will speed up the communicating system between astronauts and the control center on Earth

4) Location determination will give needed information about the surrounding environment

5) Will help in supporting the mental health of the astronauts

Predicted impacts:

Improving health care and monitoring astronauts' health during long space missions in order to elongate their trip duration.

Avoiding the sudden disconnection between astronauts and the control center.

Decreasing their risks of exposure to harsh disease.

Decrease their feeling of isolation.

Guide for the astronauts to deal with emergencies.

Help scientists with their research about the occurring changes inside the human body during their mission.

Used tools: trained Avent

Coding: HTML, CSS, payton

Hardware: smartwatch, tablets, laptop, and computer

Our project provides an offline AI assistant that helps in dealing with different solutions, such as radiation amount as a result of determining the location, decreasing feelings of isolation as a result of the existence of the assistant and decreasing the disconnection between the astronaunts and the control center.

The main factors we considered were the five main hazards, as they helped us in collecting the needed data to achieve the needed results.
